decisions.reason: Explorer reliability and data validation rules do not provide a framework that the data-to-intelligence process directly expands or applies. They share a broad data context but lack a direct structural dependency.
Concentration accounts and M&A risks are distinct specific risk topics. The definition of concentration accounts does not provide a framework that M&A risks operationalize or expand.

CH19 provides the foundational FATF framework and recommendations; CH21 expands on international anti-corruption efforts by detailing how the G-20 ACWG collaborates with and builds upon this FATF framework.
FIU intelligence admissibility limits and intelligent transaction monitoring solutions are distinct topics. One does not provide a framework that the other directly applies or expands.

CH58 defines clean data and its importance; CH51 directly applies this definition by assessing existing systems and data quality, specifically noting how poor data quality impacts next-generation technologies.
Bribery definition and M&A risks are different specific topics. M&A risks mentioning bribery laws does not mean the bribery definition CP grounds the M&A risk CP.

CH58 provides the data cleansing rules and governance framework; CH51 operationalizes this by detailing the initial assessment of existing systems and data quality as a necessary step before implementing new tools.

CH42 defines the ID&V step in the KYC process; CH47 expands on this by detailing the purpose and notification requirements for customer due diligence meetings, which is a direct operationalization of gathering ID&V information.
SAR submission actions and MLA request confidentiality are distinct procedural topics. They share a broad confidentiality theme but lack a direct structural dependency.
Environmental crime definition and UNODC AFC role are distinct topics. UNODC's general mandate does not directly expand or operationalize the specific definition of environmental crime.
